focus: Question-tool decision capture: ask-surface-guard detector accuracy, once-guard enforcement and decision-capture write paths
answeredQuestions: Question-tool capture (v4.0.2.0): do .skilled/hooks/ask-surface-guard and .skilled/hooks/decision-capture detect typed option menus as the fixtures claim, and where do they false-positive or false-negative?

label: Numbered instruction lists written 1)/2)/3) fire as prose menus: OPTION_LINE accepts 1)-9) and any question within three non-blank lines above or anywhere after the list completes the match, so a how-to list closing with a yes/no question is sent back as if it were a menu.

The commonest numbered-menu form, 1./2./3., is never detected because a number option label must be followed by ')'; the release note promises 'A/B/C or 1/2/3' menus without qualifying the separator, so together with f-iter005-001 the discriminator is punctuation-shaped rather than semantic.

A menu inside a 4-space indented code block fires, because normalization strips fenced blocks, blockquotes, tables and headings but not indented code; the same shape is proven safe by the fenced fixture code-block-menu.json.

A question more than three non-blank lines above the option list escapes detection: QUESTION_LOOKBACK is 3 and the question scan runs forward only from firstOption-3, so a menu preceded by a paragraph of context passes as no-menu.

The 'sent back once' promise is enforced per assistant message on OpenCode (marker keyed on messageId, and promptAsync creates a new message id) and per turn counter on DSH, not per operator turn as on Pi and Claude; an agent that repeats the menu can be sent back unbounded.

The Claude ask-surface adapter never passes surfaceAvailable to evaluateTurn, so the core's default of true applies even in a session where AskUserQuestion is not available; the file's safety argument covers subagents only, not an allowed-tools restriction.

An untracked .skilled/logs/cli-dispatch-audit.log tree exists inside .skilled/hooks/decision-capture, evidence that a writer resolved .skilled/logs against a cwd inside the hook folder rather than the project root; the same cwd-relative class the state writers avoid by joining an explicit root.
All 10 ask-surface fixtures reproduce their expected verdict through evaluateTurn (0 mismatches), so the fixture set is honest; the false positives come from shapes no fixture covers.

Decision answers are written to <root>/.skilled/skills/.state/decision-capture/<projectToken>/<sessionToken>.jsonl with a .nudge sibling and a per-session lock, and fires to <root>/.skilled/skills/.state/ask-surface/fires.jsonl; both under the gitignored runtime state Gate 3 exempts.

Hook suites here are node:test files that the hooks vitest config deliberately excludes; no workflow in the workflow directory listing names the ask-surface suite, so where those suites execute in CI is unconfirmed.

direction: Codex/Devin never sending the turn back is drift from the release note
reason: Both the advisory-only path (module header states Codex and Devin document no blocking decision) and the release note (Codex and Devin print a warning instead) say the same thing; this is a documented ceiling, not drift.
